ac1_proof.base_side: frozen transcriptions of the five static admission predicates exactly as they stood at a28e00656ba886288af24d9f3cd0cafd7796eb7e: P1 lsc1_packet_frontend.sv:860-861 (SET -> BAD_CELL), P2 :892-895 (DEREF -> BAD_CELL), P3 :927-931 (JUMP -> BAD_CELL), P4 :936-938 (JUMP -> BAD_BRANCH_PROPOSAL detail 3), P5 :979-983 (XOR/MUL -> BAD_CELL). Every quantity is read from the same raw bit offset of frame_payload that the base arm read it from, and the offsets are written as literal expressions copied from the frontend rather than as localparams, so a drift between the frontend and the validator's offset localparams cannot be hidden behind a shared definition.
ac1_proof.free_input_decomposition: 8 frame_opcode + 16 frame_length + 1520 frame_payload + 1 result_pending + 1 blake_result_pending + 1 blake_service_pending
ac1_proof.head_side: instantiates the shipped, unmodified lsc1_request_validator, not a transcription of it, so the proof binds the artifact compiled into the design. sha256 of the instantiated file: 0d0cee24aea05b1a2ae2691a1cc46518af79b79e6228b8bb41031394c15b8d4f, byte-identical to base.
ac1_proof.method: combinational dominance probe, complete SAT (yosys `prep -top probe_top; flatten; hierarchy -top probe_top; sat -verify -prove-asserts -set-def-inputs`). For each predicate P_X the probe exposes viol_X = !request_reject && arm_X && P_X and asserts viol_X == 1'b0.
ac1_proof.obligation: The decode ladder that carries P1..P5 sits on the `else` branch of `request_reject` (lsc1_packet_frontend.sv:768-771). If the shipped validator rejects every frame that satisfies any P_X, the ladder never evaluates P_X on an accepted frame and the five arms are unreachable. UNSAT of `!reject && arm && P_X` over the whole input space is exactly that statement.
ac1_proof.quantification: exhaustive over all 2^1547 input assignments; no input constraints, no assumptions, no abstraction
ac1_proof.solver_problem: 19410 variables, 54181 clauses (identical for all six obligations)
ac1_proof.strengthening_note: The probe's arm guards are deliberately WEAKER than the RTL's. The frontend enters an arm only when `decision_ok` still holds and only after the earlier arms of the same if/else-if chain have been excluded; P4 additionally sits behind the U32_OVERFLOW, P3 and cell_alias_inconsistent arms. Dropping those conditions enlarges the set of inputs the proof must discharge, so the UNSAT result is strictly stronger than the reachability question actually asked.

pinned_not_fixed.why: The cell scan outranking the JUMP branch-proposal check is the behaviour at a28e0065. Note that P3 and P4 -- the two frontend arms this slice deletes -- are precisely the frontend's copies of that ordering; after this slice the ordering is expressed once, in the validator, which is where the wire protocol's behaviour has always come from because the ladder sits on the `else` branch of request_reject. Changing the ordering remains a separate ticket and is explicitly not done here.

subject: Delete from asic_core/rtl/lsc1_packet_frontend.sv the five static admission predicates that the shipped lsc1_request_validator provably dominates (P1 SET :860, P2 DEREF :892, P3 JUMP :927, P4 JUMP branch-proposal :936, P5 XOR/MUL :979) together with the four scratch stores that fed only those predicates (D1 :879, D2 :913, D3 :915, D4 :917). The decode ladder carrying these arms sits on the `else` branch of request_reject, so a frame the validator accepts can never satisfy any of them; the arms are unreachable and their operand loads are dead. No module is added, no RTL file is created, and no testbench, vector or expected value is touched.
